finding: The site has no live range for this job, so there is nothing to grade; this file is a first build. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Corolla about $160-$304; midsize 2016 Camry about $160-$349; truck 2016 F-150 5.0L about $160-$360; luxury 2015 BMW 328i about $229-$490, before any battery registration. These sit close to the benchmarks: Jerry gives $268-$368 installed, a battery chain gives $185-$400 for the battery with installation often free, a mobile mechanic chain's figures add up to about $100-$370, and RepairPal shows $223-$251 for a 2021 Honda Civic. Candidly, this is a menu-priced service: the battery chain whose guide was loaded says most of its locations fit a battery free with purchase and otherwise charge $20-$75, so a real bill can be just the battery price plus tax and core, which is at or below the bottom of a parts-plus-book-time build; the top of each built range (a full hour at $160) is what a repair shop or dealer billing normal labor might reach, not what most drivers pay. How solid the numbers are: the hours are weak. No manufacturer-stated time for swapping a 12-volt battery was found (four Honda battery-related bulletins were checked and none lists one), so every class uses one general guide's 20-60 minutes, which is not specific to any of the example vehicles. Parts: the Ford and BMW high ends are genuine list prices from OEM catalogs. No Toyota TrueStart list price could be loaded, so the economy and midsize high ends are the top retail tier seen at a national retailer ($144.04 and $189.00), not OEM list, and a dealer battery may cost more. The Camry's group size and the BMW's exact battery size were not confirmed from a loaded source; the retailer's tier prices were the same across the sizes seen, which limits the error. The low ends use the retailer's mid tier ($120.51); its budget tier is $81.37. BMW battery registration: no source stating a time or price was found, so it is not included and the luxury total could be higher.
extras: A quote often adds a refundable core charge until the old battery is handed back (none of the pages loaded stated the amount, and it is left out of the prices here), a battery and charging system test, terminal cleaning or anti-corrosion treatment, shop supplies or a battery disposal fee, and sales tax. Some cars, BMW among them, need the new battery registered or coded to the car's computer, which a shop may charge for separately; no stated time or price for that was found. On some vehicles the battery sits under a seat, in the trunk or behind a wheel-well liner, which takes longer than the general times used here. A weak battery can also be a sign of a charging fault, so an alternator test may be suggested.
